subject: microbiology

resources.title: CDC Microbiology eLearning Series
resources.provider: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

resources.title: MIT 7.21 / 7.62 Microbial Physiology
resources.notes: MIT catalog documents bacterial physiology, bacteriophages, genetic and metabolic regulation, cell envelopes, secretion, pathogenesis, bioenergetics, symbiosis, quorum sensing, DNA-damage responses and biofilms. The graduate version requires greater depth.

resources.title: MIT 7.13 Experimental Microbial Genetics
resources.notes: Research-project laboratory course using molecular genetics with Pseudomonas aeruginosa, including antibiotic resistance and other microbial phenotypes.

resources.title: MIT 7.493 Microbial Genetics and Evolution
resources.notes: Graduate course covering microbial genetic/genomic analyses, central dogma, horizontal gene transfer and evolution. Research level denotes research-oriented literature/method context, not independent expert-readiness certification.

resources.title: MIT 7.492 Methods and Problems in Microbiology
resources.notes: Graduate microbiology course centered on primary literature, methods and approaches used to understand and manipulate microbes.

resources.title: CDC MicrobeNet
resources.provider: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
resources.notes: Reference/identification tool; not treated as a standalone curriculum.

resources.title: CDC DPDx Diagnostic Procedures
resources.provider: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

resources.title: CDC Infectious Disease Pathology Laboratory Techniques
resources.provider: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

resources.title: NIAID Bioinformatics Portal Training Resources
resources.provider: National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases
resources.notes: Discovery/training portal. Individual resources require item-level verification before being counted as complete instructional evidence.

known_gaps: Foundation and beginner instruction remains thin outside the CDC laboratory-training material.
Dedicated virology, mycology, parasitology and immunomicrobiology curricula need stronger level-specific instructional evidence.
Microbiome science needs dedicated course/project evidence rather than relying mainly on a training portal.
Research-oriented courses and reference tools do not by themselves establish ATLAS expert readiness; practical verification, retrieval and assessment remain required.
